question.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=2x(t)-4y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=x(t)-2y(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear differential equations above. The eigenvector corresponding to the only eigenvalue $\lambda =0$ of the system's matrix $A$ is $v=[2,\text{ }1]^{T}.$ The vector $w=[1,\text{ }0]^{T}$ is such that $(A-\lambda I)w=v.$  Which of the following could represent the phase portrait of the system?

*Hint: Here, the dotted line represents the equilibrium solutions.*
question.worked_solution:
Since we have a repeated eigenvalue $\lambda =0$ (of multiplicity two) and only one corresponding eigenvector $v,$ the solution of the system is given by

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}v{e}^{\lambda t}+{c}_{2}(vt{e}^{\lambda t}+w{e}^{\lambda t}\,),
$$

where $w$ is a solution to the equation $(A-\lambda I)w=v.$

In our case,

$$
\lambda =0,\,v=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Thus, the general solution of the system is 

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}] & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}([\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]t+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]) \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2t+1 \\ t\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.\end{aligned}
$$

First, notice that ${x}_{E}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ are equilibrium solutions of the system since ${x}_{E}^{′}(t)=0.$ These solutions form the line with the equation $y=\frac{1}{2}x$ in the phase space, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14274360/assets/5afce1bca483dbd9bd462810c351d710469b744813cd9f54ea3234f0c7343d35.png)

 

Now, we consider some general solutions of the form

$$
[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}]={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2t+1 \\ t\end{aligned}].
$$

For example:

- When ${c}_{1}=1$ and ${c}_{2}=1,$ we get the following curve:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=2t+3 \\ y=t+1\end{aligned}
$$

Let's add it to the phase space:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14274360/assets/4019f96cd3c03ec9b0349a0a896951bfa4b0b8f0f828442e002de28d7c8ceb92.png)

- When ${c}_{1}=-1$ and ${c}_{2}=-1,$ we get the following curve:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=-2t-3 \\ y=-t-1\end{aligned}
$$

Let's add it to the phase space:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14274360/assets/df4f8378d0c02f982299a349e76c204fd60fb5e014b72e01545cc5dec358aa04.png)

 

The phase portrait of our system looks as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14274360/assets/1871e29694b88593a1aeb9ac87536059361f30a2e39966a9ca1180067213d15c.png)
